## The sequence

**Reversed 30 Aug 2026.** The old order is kept below the new one, because tickets and code both referred to it.

```
9a Welcome
  → 9b Apple sheet
  → 9c Verifying
  → 9e six questions
  → 9f your targets
  → Today
  → 9g first capture        (doc 27)
  → 9j first review         (doc 27)
```

Was, until 30 Aug 2026:

```
9a → 9b → 9c → 9g first capture → 9j first review → 9d bridge → 9e six questions → 9f targets → Today
```

Auth is three screens where it was four, and only one of them is ours. Onboarding sits *before* the first logged meal, and there is no way past it.

---

## What changed, and why the screens changed with it

### Auth is one action

Register and login are the same call, so the Register / Log in toggle on `6b` was answering a question the user is no longer asked. Welcome is now a wordmark, a sentence and one button.

The copy under the button does the work the toggle used to: *signing in and signing up are the same action*. Without it, a returning user hesitates over whether they are about to make a second account.

### The Apple sheet is drawn even though it is not ours

Two reasons. It is a screen the user unambiguously sees, so leaving it out makes the sequence read shorter than it is. And the **Hide My Email** row is the visual argument for the `apple_user_id` join key — the one detail on this path that is expensive to get wrong.

The annotation on `9b` names the first-authorization trap directly: name and email arrive **only** on that first authorization. It is a bug that is invisible until the second user signs in, and impossible to fix retroactively.

### Verifying is a real screen, not a spinner

A second or two of JWKS fetch, signature validation and claim checks, drawn as three named lines rather than an indeterminate spinner — same principle as the analyze state in doc 06. A frozen view during a slow call reads as a crash.

It also replaces the entire verify-email stack, and with it the trap doc 04 describes: a blocking email inside an unexitable onboarding stack, where an undelivered message left a user with no path forward.

### The bridge screen, deleted 30 Aug 2026

`9d` did not exist in any prior doc. The resequencing invented it, to design the moment where a user who had just watched a photo turn into three numbers gets asked for six answers. It showed **their own first entry at the top**, so the payoff sat directly above the ask, and its *Not now* was a real exit that stated its cost.

All of that was good work on a premise that no longer holds. With the questions first there is no first entry to show and no gap to bridge, so the screen is gone and the exit with it.

What survives is the reason it was drawn. **An ask needs a reason next to it.** The questions still need that sentence, and where it lives is the open question noted in the screen table above.

### Six questions, not ten

Goal weight, timeline, training days and dietary constraints are gone — none are inputs to Mifflin-St Jeor. The screen is otherwise unchanged from `6e`, minus the free-text control, which existed only for the dietary-constraints question. The `isText` branch has been removed from the component rather than left dormant.

---

## Decisions

**The stack is unexitable, again.** Reversed 30 Aug 2026. This doc briefly made it exitable, reasoning that a user with entries and no targets is a coherent state. With the questions first that state is unreachable, so doc 21's original description is right after all: flow 01 is a modal you cannot leave. Back from question one goes nowhere, because there is nothing behind it.

That is a trap shape, and this doc names the same trap two sections above, in the verify-email stack it deleted. The difference is that all six questions are answerable offline. Nothing inside the stack waits on a network call except the final target write, and doc 18's deterministic fallback covers the AI step. **Any future step that can block must not go inside this stack.**

The client enforces it in two places, not one. A deep link to Today never runs the launch gate, so the guard on every signed-in route checks it as well.

**Welcome carries no legal wall.** One line about photos going to an AI provider, in the dimmest text on the screen. It is true, it is the only surprising thing about the data flow, and it belongs before the tap rather than in a settings page.

**No returning-user variant of Welcome.** The button is identical either way; the server decides. Drawing two states that differ in nothing would imply a branch the code does not have.

## Gaps and open questions

**Where does 9d's "why we are asking" sentence go?** Open. See the screen inventory.

**What does 9c hand off to now?** It ended on `LOG YOUR FIRST MEAL` and pushed into capture. With the questions first it has to hand off to `9e`, and the copy needs redrawing.

**Resolved 30 Aug 2026 by the sequencing reversal:**

* *The camera prompt arriving four seconds after install.* It now arrives after six questions and a targets screen, which is the context doc 06 asked for.
* Backfilling null `target_version` *is invisible.* There is no null to backfill. The column is NOT NULL and no day can exist before targets do.
* *Skipping targets has no second prompt.* There is no skip.
